text:
emma: Heads up — NimbusHealth is ready to convert the POC into a PO. They've submitted MSA/DPA redlines and a request to change payment to Net60. Need quick alignment on: prepay, SLA for POC, and who can sign the order form. cc @linda @mike @adarsh

linda: I skimmed the redlines. They remove our audit and data-retention protections — can't accept as-is. I can draft a one-page POC addendum that limits scope (data deletion + limited audit rights) and keeps our standard DPA for production.

mike: Procurement note — they'll send a formal PO but prefer Net60. For us, finance usually requires Net30 or Net45 depending on risk. Also need remit address + tax info on the PO.

olivia: Finance: For a short POC we typically require either prepay or a purchase order with credit approved. Net60 is a hard no unless credit review passes. I can approve Net45 + 50% prepayment for this account pending credit check.

emma: Product/SE context: POC will run on dedicated capacity for ~2 weeks, expected peak ~50 req/s. Concurrency may spike during load tests. Can we mark the SLA as non-binding for POC? @adarsh any concerns?

adarsh: SE — performance-wise 50 req/s on dedicated is fine. But we can't commit to 99.9% latency SLO for a short-term POC. Recommend a "POC performance objective" (example: median latency <150ms) and include a short perf-test annex. I'll run a perf run Monday and paste results.

sec-bot: Security questionnaire landed from NimbusHealth: https://redwood-secure/qs/3742 Please fill. They flagged encryption-at-rest HSM requirement — we can provide KMS attestation for POC but not customer-managed HSM for a temporary evaluation.

linda: On signatures: we can accept e-sign by an authorized procurement rep + PO attachment. I'll add a clause to the order form: "Order Form shall be signed by an authorized representative of Buyer and include the Buyer PO# if applicable." Also adding data deletion (30 days) to the POC addendum.

mike: Procurement asks: would Sales accept Net45 + 50% prepay? They'll try to push for milestone payments, but that adds complexity. Also confirm invoice remit and W-9 requirement.

olivia: Confirmed: I can greenlight Net45 + 50% prepay for this POC once we have billing contact and credit hygiene. If they insist on Net60 we need explicit PO and an approved credit exception.

emma: Drafting proposal => 1) 1-page POC addendum (legal) 2) 50% prepay, remainder Net45 3) SLA labeled "POC performance objective" (non-binding) 4) E-sign allowed with PO attachment. Sound good?

adarsh: Sounds good. I'll run perf Monday and attach results; if median <150ms we'll use that as the objective in the addendum.

linda: I'll produce the POC addendum today and circulate for quick sign-off. Will preserve audit right for limited-scope checks and include 30-day data deletion. I will also remove any blanket HSM requirement for POC.

raj: AE — I'll notify the customer of the 50% prepay requirement and ask them to route PO to procurement@redwood.example. I'll collect their billing contact and PO# so Finance can proceed.

emma: Action items recap: @linda draft addendum and update DPA redlines; @adarsh perf run Mon; @mike confirm PO remittance details; @olivia confirm Net45 + prepay; @raj tell the customer. I'll own the e-sign envelope and attach the addendum when ready. :thumbsup:

emma: Quick snippet I plan to include in the order form:
```
Term: POC (2 weeks)
Payment: 50% prepay, remainder Net45 from invoice date
SLA: POC performance objective (non-binding) — median latency target 150ms
Data: Data deletion within 30 days after POC
```

emma: If anyone objects to the prepay ask or the non-binding SLA language now is the time to flag it, otherwise I'll push these changes to the customer and route the addendum for e-sign.
